hypothesis: A two-shuffle XOR butterfly over the four shared warp totals may reduce cross-warp combine work relative to the prior five-step warp reduction or serial lane-0 sum. This changes only the block-local combine while retaining 128-element tiles, recursive host stages, and modulo-2^32 partials; the full-program measurements do not establish that local reduction is the bottleneck.

transformations: Replaced the modulo/shared-memory reduction tree with five warp-local shuffle-down additions, one shared unsigned total per warp, and a two-stage XOR butterfly across the four totals in warp zero.

Used unsigned modulo-2^32 addition for all partial sums and mapped each residue to an in-range signed int before storing it, so recursive stages recover the same residue without out-of-range signed conversion.
Kept 128-thread blocks, zero-filled tail handling, the existing alternating scratch-bank offsets, recursive host launches, ABI, and default-stream ordering; writes zero asynchronously for n <= 0.
